title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 3 of a set of lecture or seminar notes, apparently recording a 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. It continues the previous page, which identified the homology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces with derived functors of Sym via Dold–Thom and Dold–Puppe. This page moves to mod-p cohomology operations and the Steenrod algebra.

(1) Mod-p cohomology of K(F_p,n) is the linear dual of mod-p homology: H^{n+r}(K(F_p,n),F_p) ≅ H_{n+r}(K(F_p,n),F_p)^*. The fibration K(Z,n) → K(Z,n) → K(F_p,n), induced by multiplication by p, relates the integral and mod-p cases.

(2) Representability. K(F_p,n) represents H^n(-,F_p). Hence cohomology operations of type (F_p,n; F_p,n+r) correspond to H^{n+r}(K(F_p,n),F_p).

(3) Stable operations of degree r. These are families {P_n : H^n(X,F_p) → H^{n+r}(X,F_p)}, one for every n, that commute with the suspension isomorphism H̃^{n+1}(SX) ≅ H̃^n(X).

(4) Stable range. For r < n the cohomology suspension gives H^{n+r}(K(F_p,n)) ≅ H^{n+r+1}(K(F_p,n+1)), a Freudenthal / Serre stability statement. So in this range every operation is the restriction of a unique stable one.

(5) The stable operations form the Steenrod algebra.
- For p ≠ 2 it is generated by P^0 = 1, P^i of degree 2i(p−1), and the Bockstein β of degree 1, subject to the Adem relations.
- The reference given is Steenrod–Epstein, 'Cohomology Operations', Annals of Mathematics Studies 50, Princeton, p. 77.

The point of this material in the lecture's context: the next page states Serre's computation of H^*(K(F_p,n)) as a free graded-commutative algebra on admissible monomials, and dually describes the homology as a divided-power algebra. This is the topological input for comparing the derived functors of Sym and Γ with the divided-power de Rham complex (the Dold–Puppe, Cartan and Breen circle of ideas).
errors: The first line writes H_*( )^* ≅ H^{n+r}; the correct degreewise statement is H_{n+r}(K(F_p,n),F_p)^* ≅ H^{n+r}(K(F_p,n),F_p). This is a notational slip.

Writing the Steenrod algebra as 'F_p[P^0, P^1, …, β]' suggests a polynomial (commutative) algebra. It is really the free associative algebra on these generators modulo the Adem relations, and it is non-commutative.

Minor: the stable range r < n is stated correctly. The suspension map is an isomorphism for n+r < 2n, and in the boundary case one needs some care (surjectivity only). This is not elaborated in the notes.

transcription_corrections: Line 1 is better read as H_{n+r}(K(F_p,n),F_p)^* ≅ H^{n+r}(K(F_p,n),F_p); the image has H_* with a dual star.
The phrase 'représente la F_p-coh' reads as 'représente la F_p-cohomologie', i.e. K(F_p,n) represents mod-p cohomology.
